description: Probe set of 10 tasks spanning nominal, ordinal, and free-form candidate rubrics per claude_gap.md Phase 1A.

tasks.state: Customer says: My credit card was charged $45.00 twice on September 15th for order #1234. Please issue a refund.
tasks.instructions: Route the ticket to the responsible department.

candidates.description: Payment inquiries, double charges, refunds, and invoice disputes.
Software bugs, website crashes, login failures, and API errors.
Tracking packages, customs delays, physical damage during transit.
Password resets, profile updates, account closure requests.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Does the issue involve money, charges, or invoices? If YES -> billing. Step 2: Does it involve software or system errors? If YES -> technical. Step 3: Does it involve delivery? If YES -> shipping. Else -> account.

exemplars_8shot.state: I see an unknown $10 charge.
The page crashes on login.
My package hasn't arrived.
Change my email address.
Refund my canceled flight.
API returns 500 error code.
Box was crushed when delivered.
I forgot my password.

tasks.state: Customer says: I no longer need this subscription service. How do I permanently cancel my membership before renewal?

candidates.description: User requests to cancel, terminate, or stop an existing subscription or service.
User requests to temporarily pause, freeze, or hold their account.
User wants to renew, extend, or upgrade their current subscription plan.
User is providing general feedback or complaints without asking for changes.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Is user asking to end/stop membership completely? If YES -> cancel_service. Step 2: Is user asking for temporary freeze? If YES -> pause_service. Step 3: Is user renewing? If YES -> renew_service. Else -> feedback.

exemplars_8shot.state: Cancel my Pro plan immediately.
Hold my gym membership for 1 month.
I want to sign up for another year.
Your UI looks outdated.
Stop charging me and close my account.
Freeze subscription while I travel.
Extend my trial period please.
Customer support was very friendly.

tasks.state: Applicant is 24 years old, holds a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, and has 3 years of commercial Python experience.
tasks.instructions: Assess applicant qualification category for Senior Software Engineer.

candidates.description: Meets or exceeds all required technical qualifications and seniority (>= 5 years exp).
Has relevant degree but lacks required minimum years of senior experience (< 5 years).
Lacks relevant degree or domain background entirely.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Does candidate have a CS/related degree? If NO -> unrelated. Step 2: Does candidate have >= 5 years experience? If YES -> eligible. If NO (< 5 years) -> underqualified.

exemplars_8shot.state: CS degree, 6 years experience.
History degree, no programming experience.
CS degree, 2 years experience.
SE degree, 8 years Python experience.
Literature degree, no tech background.
CS degree, 4 years experience.
Math degree, 7 years experience.
Culinary arts diploma.

tasks.state: The essay presents a clear thesis in paragraph 1, provides three supporting paragraphs each with distinct topic sentences and transition phrases ('Furthermore', 'In contrast'), and concludes with a synthesis of main points.
tasks.instructions: Assign the structural organization score according to the ordinal rubric.

candidates.description: Level 1: No discernible structure; ideas are disconnected and lack sequencing.
Level 2: Basic attempt at grouping, but transitions are absent and order is confusing.
Level 3: Competent structure with clear beginning/middle/end, but mechanical transitions.
Level 4: Fluent, cohesive organization with sophisticated transitions and effective progression.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Is there a clear thesis, distinct topical paragraphs, and conclusion? If NO -> score_1 or score_2. Step 2: Are transitions present and effectively connecting paragraphs? If basic/mechanical -> score_3. If fluent and cohesive -> score_4.

exemplars_8shot.state: Sentences are in random order with no paragraphs.
Has two big paragraphs but jump between topics abruptly.
Has intro, body, conclusion, uses First, Second, Third.
Seamless transitions connecting nuanced arguments across paragraphs.
No punctuation or paragraph breaks.
Some grouping but the conclusion is in the middle.
Standard five-paragraph essay structure followed strictly.
Masterful pacing and flow across thematic sections.

tasks.state: Production database cluster experienced 15 minutes of degraded query latency, impacting approximately 2% of user requests. No data loss occurred and all requests eventually succeeded.
tasks.instructions: Determine the operational incident severity tier.

candidates.description: SEV-1 (Critical): Total service outage impacting >50% users, or verified data loss.
SEV-2 (Major): Core feature unavailable for significant fraction of users (>10%).
SEV-3 (Minor): Partial degradation or non-critical feature affected (<10% users).
SEV-4 (Low): Cosmetic bug or internal annoyance with zero user-visible degradation.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Was there total outage (>50%) or data loss? If YES -> sev_1. Step 2: Was core feature down for >10%? If YES -> sev_2. Step 3: Was user-visible latency/performance degraded for <10%? If YES -> sev_3. Step 4: No user impact? If YES -> sev_4.

exemplars_8shot.state: Entire site returns 503 error for 2 hours.
Checkout button broken for all European users (25%).
Search latency increased for 3% of queries.
Typo in footer link on terms page.
Database dropped tables, permanent loss.
Payment gateway failing for 15% of transactions.
Dashboard load time slow for small group of admins.
Log formatting error in background job.

tasks.state: The PR implements the requested feature and includes basic unit tests, but lacks docstrings, has two variable names with single letters, and ignores a lint warning about line length.
tasks.instructions: Rate the code review quality band according to the rubric.

candidates.description: Band 1: Non-functional, untested, or fundamentally flawed architecture.
Band 2: Functional and tested, but contains style defects, missing docs, or minor lints.
Band 3: Thoroughly tested, documented, clean architecture, adhering to all standards.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Does the code work and have tests? If NO -> needs_rework. Step 2: Are there minor style defects, missing docs, or lint issues? If YES -> acceptable. If completely clean and documented -> exemplary.

exemplars_8shot.state: Code does not compile and has syntax error.
Works with tests, but variable names are x, y and no docs.
Flawless code with 100% test coverage and full docstrings.
Fails runtime on edge case, zero tests.
Passes tests but has commented-out dead code.
Elegant design, comprehensive tests, clean documentation.
PR breaks existing build.
Feature works, just needs variable renaming.

tasks.state: Patient presents with a 2 cm superficial laceration on left forearm, bleeding controlled with direct pressure, normal vital signs, alert and oriented.
tasks.instructions: Assign the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) triage level.

candidates.description: Level 1: Resuscitation needed; immediate life-saving intervention required.
Level 2: Emergent; high risk, confused/lethargic, severe pain/distress.
Level 3: Urgent; normal vitals but requires two or more hospital resources.
Level 4: Less urgent; stable, requires exactly one resource (e.g. simple suture or X-ray).
Level 5: Non-urgent; stable, requires no medical intervention beyond exam/prescription.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Life-saving intervention required? If YES -> esi_1. Step 2: High risk / confused? If YES -> esi_2. Step 3: Resource count? 2+ resources -> esi_3. Exactly 1 resource (sutures) -> esi_4. 0 resources -> esi_5.

exemplars_8shot.state: Cardiac arrest, unresponsiveness.
Severe chest pain, diaphoresis, high risk.
Abdominal pain requiring blood tests and CT scan.
Simple finger cut needing 3 stitches.
Need prescription refill, no acute symptoms.
Gunshot wound, severe hemorrhage, shock.
Suspected stroke, sudden facial droop.
Clean laceration needing closure.

tasks.state: A company headquartered in Frankfurt collects personal data from German citizens to deliver a mobile fitness application, storing data on AWS servers located in Frankfurt.
tasks.instructions: Determine the governing data protection framework based on legal scope criteria.

candidates.description: Criterion: Processing of EU personal data by an EU-established controller without cross-border US/UK transfers.
Criterion: Processing consumer data of California residents with gross revenue > $25M.
Criterion: Processing personal data of United Kingdom data subjects under the Data Protection Act 2018.
Criterion: Involves conflicting requirements across three or more divergent national jurisdictions.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Is controller established in EU processing EU citizen data exclusively in EU? If YES -> gdpr_exclusive. Step 2: Does it involve California residents? If YES -> ccpa_applicable. Step 3: Does it involve UK data subjects? If YES -> uk_gdpr. Else -> multinational_conflict.

exemplars_8shot.state: Berlin startup storing German user profiles in Munich.
Los Angeles retailer selling to San Francisco shoppers.
London firm processing Manchester patient records.
Global bank syncing data between Tokyo, Zurich, and New York.
Paris bakery app for local French customers.
San Diego company tracking California web visitors.
Edinburgh agency handling Scottish records.
Multinational conglomerate across 15 countries.

tasks.state: Premise: Two children in bright yellow raincoats are splashing through puddles on an asphalt playground while holding red umbrellas.
tasks.instructions: Determine the logical relationship to the hypothesis: 'Children are outdoors playing in the rain.'

candidates.description: The hypothesis must necessarily be true given the facts stated in the premise.
The hypothesis cannot be true under any circumstances if the premise is true.
The hypothesis could be true or false; the premise provides insufficient evidence to guarantee it.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Does puddles + raincoats + outdoors necessarily require playing in rain? If YES -> entailment. Step 2: Does the hypothesis contradict the premise? If YES -> contradiction. Step 3: Is it merely plausible but unproven? If YES -> neutral.

exemplars_8shot.state: Premise: A dog is running in the park. Hypothesis: An animal is outside.
Premise: The man is asleep in bed. Hypothesis: The man is running a marathon.
Premise: A woman is eating an apple. Hypothesis: The woman loves fruit.
Premise: Three students are taking an exam. Hypothesis: People are in a classroom.
Premise: The car is parked in the garage. Hypothesis: The car is driving on the highway.
Premise: A boy is reading a book. Hypothesis: The book is about science.
Premise: A swimmer dives into the pool. Hypothesis: A person enters water.
Premise: The room is completely empty. Hypothesis: Five people are talking in the room.

tasks.state: The user writes: 'When I try to export my financial report to CSV, the system displays Error 504 Gateway Timeout after 60 seconds.'
tasks.instructions: Route according to technical support SLA boundary criteria.

candidates.description: Server gateway timeouts, proxy drops, database connection pool exhaustion, or HTTP 504 errors.
CSV parsing syntax errors, column truncation, or incorrect formula calculations on valid exports.
HTTP 401/403 authorization failures or missing user export privileges.
Browser extension conflicts, local network disconnections, or operating system file locks.

tasks.decision_tree: Step 1: Is there a 504 Gateway Timeout or proxy drop? If YES -> infrastructure_sla. Step 2: Is it a logic/format bug in the CSV? If YES -> application_defect. Step 3: Auth error (401/403)? If YES -> permission_denied. Step 4: Local client bug? If YES -> client_environment.

exemplars_8shot.state: Nginx returns 504 Gateway Time-out on heavy queries.
Exported CSV puts numbers in wrong columns.
You do not have permission to view this report (403).
Chrome crashes when opening file dialog on macOS.
Upstream server timed out after 30 seconds.
Date column has NaN instead of actual dates.
Invalid token error on request.
Ad blocker prevents the download button from clicking.
